    Quickstart

    Install wayu, add its one line to your shell, and move your first PATH entries, aliases and secrets into it. Every command, flag and exit code is in the CLI reference; every config key in the configuration reference.

    Install#

    Homebrew (macOS 15 or later on Apple silicon or Intel, Linux on x86_64 or arm64):

    brew tap dvrd/wayu
brew install wayu
wayu init

    Or the install script, on the same platforms without Homebrew:

    curl -fsSL https://wayu.dvrd.io/install.sh | sh
wayu init

    It downloads the release archive for your OS and CPU, checks its SHA-256 (and its build provenance attestation when the GitHub CLI gh is installed and logged in), and installs wayu to ~/.local/bin, replacing an older one atomically. WAYU_VERSION=v7.0.0 installs that release, WAYU_INSTALL_DIR another directory. It refuses to install next to a Homebrew-managed wayu (WAYU_FORCE=1 overrides), and says when the directory is not on your PATH. To upgrade, run it again. Read it first if you like: install.sh.

    Other platforms (older macOS, musl Linux, the BSDs) build from source. It needs the Odin compiler at the release named in .github/odin-release:

    git clone https://github.com/dvrd/wayu && cd wayu
odin build build -out:build_it && ./build_it install   # installs to ~/.local/bin, runs wayu init

    Use one install method: while Homebrew manages wayu, ./build_it install and the install script refuse to run.

    Set up your shell#

    wayu init creates ~/.config/wayu/ (wayu.toml and the other files you edit) and ~/.local/share/wayu/ (your entries and the generated files), and offers to add one line to your rc file, or prints it when stdin is not a terminal:

    Shell rc file Line
    zsh ${ZDOTDIR:-~}/.zshrc source "${WAYU_DATA_DIR:-${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/wayu}/init.zsh"
    bash ~/.bash_profile if it exists, else ~/.bashrc source "${WAYU_DATA_DIR:-${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/wayu}/init.bash"
    fish ~/.config/fish/config.fish if test -n "$WAYU_DATA_DIR"; source $WAYU_DATA_DIR/init.fish; else if test -n "$XDG_DATA_HOME"; source $XDG_DATA_HOME/wayu/init.fish; else; source ~/.local/share/wayu/init.fish; end

    The shell is detected from $SHELL; wayu init --shell bash (or zsh, fish) picks another one. Run it once per shell you use: they share one wayu.toml and one set of entries. Open a new shell afterwards.

    First commands#

    # PATH entries: open shells pick them up at their next prompt
wayu path add ~/.cargo/bin
wayu path list

# Aliases and constants (exported variables)
wayu alias add gs 'git status -sb'
wayu const add EDITOR nvim

# An encrypted secret: the value is read with hidden input
wayu const add OPENAI_API_KEY --secret

# A secret only one command gets, never exported to the shell
wayu const add GH_TOKEN --run-only
wayu secrets run GH_TOKEN -- gh auth status

# Plugins, from the registry or a git URL
wayu plugin add autosuggestions

# Check the whole setup
wayu doctor

    Running wayu with no arguments opens the full-screen TUI. Every write is backed up first: wayu backup list shows the backups, and wayu backup restore entries --yes undoes the last change to your entries.

    Bring over an existing rc file#

    Lines that installers appended to your .zshrc (eval "$(tool init zsh)", source <(tool completion zsh), fpath edits, PATH exports, aliases) can move into wayu, where they are cached:

    wayu optimize --dry-run   # the diff and the list of what would move
wayu optimize --yes       # back the file up, rewrite it, update wayu

    Only top-level lines after wayu's own line are touched; wayu backup restore .zshrc --yes undoes it.
